canonical.name: A PCP match concatenates whole domino top and bottom strings in the chosen tile order; it never permutes symbols inside a tile.
The standard paired top-grammar and bottom-grammar construction turns a PCP instance into two CFGs whose intersection is nonempty exactly when the instance has a match.
Comparing a grammar with a fixed grammar for all strings over the same alphabet reduces CFG universality to CFG equivalence.
Even though every context-free language has decidable membership, the problem of deciding whether two CFGs generate languages with empty intersection is still undecidable.

canonical.name: A numbering treats program indices intensionally: a computable program transformer is a total computable map on indices rather than on extensional partial functions themselves.
The diagonal fixed-point construction extracted from s-m-n is the intermediate step that turns a computable transformer into an actual self-referential index.
Program indices are not unique names of partial computable functions: specialization or harmless padding can change the index while preserving the computed function.
The fixed-point mechanism behind the recursion theorem uses numbering and effective specialization, not reflective access to literal source files.
